PyTorch does not guarantee bitwise equality between CPU and CUDA, batched and sliced computations, or different releases: floating-point reduction order and kernel selection affect results. TF32 can reduce internal precision despite FP32 outputs. Therefore, small score differences alone do not establish a deployment defect. [Numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html). Scaled dot-product attention automatically selects backends whose outputs can differ; `sdpa_kernel` allows controlled comparisons. Explicitly pass `dropout_p=0.0` during evaluation: SDPA applies its specified dropout even when the enclosing model is in evaluation mode. [SDPA documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention.html).

Recommended differential testing: compare the trained module and exported predictor using identical checkpoints, histories, candidates, padding, and readout; repeat on the actual host CUDA device, software versions, dtype, autocast/TF32 settings, attention backend, and batch shapes. Compare intermediate features and final scores, including singleton versus batched inference. Use explicit absolute/relative tolerances and report maximum errors and nonfinite values; `assert_close` checks `|actual−expected| ≤ atol + rtol·|expected|`. CPU agreement is useful evidence but cannot validate the host CUDA path. Deterministic algorithms improve repeatability on the same hardware/software; they do not establish cross-device equality. [Testing](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/testing.html), [Deterministic algorithms](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.use_deterministic_algorithms.html).

Inspect ranking margins separately: `topk` does not guarantee stable indices for exact ties. As a derived diagnostic, if every score changes by at most ε, a kth-versus-(k+1)th gap exceeding 2ε protects top-k membership; smaller gaps can explain changes without an implementation defect. Investigate mismatches with large margins and preserve the pinned evaluator’s tie behavior. [Top-k documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.topk.html).
